known.title: Standard: Tests own and clean up every process they start
Gate: a successful API fast test runs the browser suite

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Standard
The standard says tests must “own and clean up every process they start, even after a crash.” This detached fast-test process is stopped only for its own `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The enclosing helper’s `finally` tracks the earlier full-test process, not this one (`tests/test_starter_tree.py:349-351`). If pytest’s 1,800-second limit or an interrupt occurs during the fast run, it can continue while the helper tears down the same Docker project. The per-test process check scans a different temporary folder; session-wide cleanup occurs only later (`tests/conftest.py:413-429`).
Case: normal use - a developer interrupts the long live smoke run, or it reaches the pytest timeout during the second command.
Adds work: stop the fast-test process group on interruption; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Standard: Tests own and clean up every process they start

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
The API-change selection test only checks that `test:browser` appears in `--list` output (`tests/test_affected_py_starter.py:44`). The real fast run deliberately stops at a TypeScript error (`tests/test_starter_tree.py:385-387`), before the browser command at `scripts/test.mjs:72`; the full smoke uses the separate no-base branch. For example, changing the fast command to the nonexistent script `test:browser-typo` would retain the checked substring and pass the negative regression, while compatible API changes fail instead of running browser tests.
Case: normal use - a compatible change under `apps/api/app/` should complete the fast test with browser coverage.
findings.title: Gate: a successful API fast test runs the browser suite

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 4 (floor: migration)
Raise: Test
This proof does not check the complete stack rule. Removing “commit them” from the migrations and lock-files sentence leaves the asserted fragment intact, even though the guidance no longer tells workers to keep those records in Git. The tracked-file check also accepts a script-generated file such as `libs/generated/client/index.ts`, since it checks only `node_modules`, `.gen.` and OpenAPI JSON names. Both regressions violate item 3 while this test stays green.
Case: normal use - a worker relies on the shipped stack guidance or a TypeScript starter gains a generated artifact.
findings.title: Gate: test_3_generated_files_stay_out_of_git_for_both_stacks
